correctness.rationale: For a positive bipartition concurrence, the source identity (Delta A_i)^2=sum_{k<l} lambda_k lambda_l(lambda_k-lambda_l)^2 is strictly below sum lambda_k lambda_l=C_i^2/4 because every contributing pair has both eigenvalues positive and hence |lambda_k-lambda_l|<1. Thus every positive cut has strict speed below sqrt(F_Q) when F_Q>0. At C_N>0, differentiating C_N^2 avoids any issue from individual zero-cut cusps: zero cuts contribute zero first derivative of their nonnegative squared concurrence, while at least one positive cut contributes strictly, giving the global strict bound. At C_N=0, existence of the ordinary derivative of the nonnegative function C_N forces it to be zero. QFI zero implies no projective state speed, hence zero concurrence speed. The GHZ family C_N=|sin 2theta|, F_Q=4 has interior ratio |cos 2theta|<1 and one-sided slopes of magnitude two at its nondifferentiable product cusps. The verifier checks only this illustration; the proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: The defining primary paper already performs the decisive saturation analysis: it explicitly states that the spectral inequality is never exactly saturated at any point with positive bipartite concurrence, only approached as concurrence tends to zero; it then says exact saturation of the general multipartite bound is confined to the product-state boundary. In the very example described as 'touched exactly', the same figure caption explicitly marks the product points as points where the derivative does not exist and states that the derivative merely approaches the envelope. The submitted theorem adds only the elementary observation that a differentiable nonnegative function has derivative zero at a zero, so it is a direct clarification of an internal wording inconsistency, not an original scientific theorem under the required bar.

final_claim: For the generalized-concurrence QFI speed bound of arXiv:2609.31853v1, at every point where the ordinary two-sided derivative exists, equality with sqrt(F_Q) is impossible when F_Q>0; equality can occur only trivially at F_Q=0, while product-state envelope contact is limiting or one-sided because the ordinary derivative fails to exist in the displayed cusp examples.
